Qedushtaot Cycle for Yom Meturgeman (Translator’s Day) on 8 Tevet

tei:div.tei:head: Qedushtaot Cycle for Yom Meturgeman (Translator’s Day) on 8 Tevet

tei:lg.tei:l: Magen
Blessed are You,
CAUSE, Our God and God of our ancestors.
God of Abraham,
God of Isaac,
and God of Jacob.
Deity, great and mighty and awesome;
Almighty Deity,
who well repays kindness,
and possesses all,
and remembers the kindnesses of ancestors
and sends a redeemer to their descendants
for the Name’s Sake, in love.
Sovereign, Help
and Rescue and Shield—
Seventy nations per their language
received Babelwards due to their iniquity.
You paid back the father of nations in their multitudes
with sacred words to guard as their own pupil.
Behold us, his children, wearing blue fringe,
and we have separated between holy speech and profane.
Our songs are in your language, with drums and dance.
You had mercy on him and increased us as sand.
Impure are the lands to which we were exiled!
We Jews were forced to change our mouths.
Each people’s language and their words we pronounced,
thus we appointed a man we call the Translator.
As written:
Thus THEY called its name Babel,
for there the CAUSE babbled the speech of all the land,
and from there the CAUSE scattered them over the face of all the earth. (Genesis 11:9)
And said:
No longer will your name be called Abram,
but your name will be Abraham,
for a father of a multitude of nations I have given you. (Genesis 17:5)
And said:
For I will bless, bless you, and increase, increase your seed
like the stars of heaven and like the sand that is by the seashore,
and your seed will inherit its enemy’s gate. (Genesis 22:17)
And said:
And they will teach My people between holy and profane,
and make them know between impure and pure. (Ezekiel 44:23)
And said:
Praise THEM with drum and dance,
praise THEM with pipe and flute! (Psalms 150:4)
And said:
How can we sing the song of the CAUSE on foreign soil? (Psalms 137:4)
And said:
And he sent out books to all the king’s provinces,
to each and every province in its script,
and to each and every people in its language,
that each man should rule his house and speak in his people’s language. (Esther 1:22)
In his people’s language the Translator explains
lest from Your wisdom the Specific People be deafened.
Shield us, Maker of each structure and root!
Blessed are You, CAUSE, Shield of Abraham.
Meḥaye
You are mighty forever, Master,
You enliven the dead, greatly saving.
You change the wind and bring down the rain.
You provide for life in kindness,
enliven the dead in great mercy,
lift the fallen, heal the sick,
free the bound,
and keep faith with sleepers in the dust.
Who is like you, Master of Powerful Acts,
and who can be compared to you?
Sovereign, who brings death and life
and causes salvation to sprout.
And trusted are You to enliven the dead—
Malachi the scribe of the Teaching was called,
who gave it script and language to bring it to light.
A worthy scribe, had it not already occured —
Ezra the priest and scribe.
The letter’s copy was given in his hand —
command Your people to explain their splendor.
He read with the Tirshatha from the book of THEIR glory;
all the people saw and rejoiced where they stood.
The sanctum’s attendants at the time of the voice’s call,
giving it sense, they understood the scripture.
They translated Your pure command —
a set translation to the end of the song.
As written:
And Moses spoke in the ears of all the community of Israel
the words of this song until their end. (Deuteronomy 31:30)
And said:
The burden of the word of the CAUSE to Israel by the hand of Malachi. (Malachi 1:1)
And said:
And this copy of the letter which the king Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest-scribe,
scribe of the words of the commandments of the CAUSE and THEIR laws upon Israel. (Ezra 7:11)
And said:
And they read in the book, in the teaching of God, explained,
and giving it sense, they understood the scripture. (Nehemiah 8:8)
And said:
And Nehemiah the Tirshatha and Ezra the priest-scribe and the levites making the people understand said to all the people:
This day is holy to the CAUSE your God,
do not mourn nor weep!
(For all the people was weeping when they heard the words of the Teaching.) (Nehemiah 8:9)
And said:
And all the people went to eat and drink and give gifts and make a great rejoicing
for they understood the words that were made known to them. (Nehemiah 8:12)
And said:
The precepts of the CAUSE are upright, gladdening the heart;
the command of the CAUSE is pure, enlightening the eyes. (Psalms 19:10)
Eyes the Translator opens
like the dew of Your Sayings, taking a good lesson.
Enliven us, Rainmaker, Healer, and Curer!
Blessed are You, CAUSE, who enlivens the dead.
Meshalesh
Greece arose and the bear was conquered.
The righteous one greeted him clad in priesthood.
He grew sick and died and was mummified in honey.
Ptolemy’s kingdom grew and consolidated.
He said, “I acquired for myself a collection of all wisdom;
philosophical ideas from all the land.
But the books of the Graced One are not in my hand.
Bring them to my palace so I may know why!
They brought him seventy elders of Israel
in order to translate the books of the Deity.
Lo, one man per room, no questions to ask;
the Redeemer did for them and us a wonder!
As written:
And now, truth I will tell you:
behold three more kings will stand for Persia,
and the fourth will be greatly enriched over all,
and per his power in wealth he will rouse all against the kingdom of Greece. (Daniel 11:2)
And said:
And a great king will stand and rule from great rule and do what he wants. (Daniel 11:3)
And said:
And I set my mind to know wisdom and knowledge of folly and foolishness;
I knew that this was also an idea of wind. (Ecclesiastes 1:17)
And said:
Say of your brothers, “My people,”
and of your sisters, “Graced one!” (Hosea 2:3)
And said:
And wisdom, from where is it found?
And what is the place of understanding? (Job 28:12)
And said:
And said to humankind:
Lo, reverence of the Master is wisdom,
and fleeing evil understanding! (Job 28:28)
And said:
A psalm. Sing to the CAUSE a new song,
for THEY did wonders;
THEIR right hand and THEIR holy arm salvations! (Psalms 98:1)
And said:
The CAUSE reigns forever;
your God, Ẓion, from generation to generation;
And You are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel. (Psalm 22:4)
El-Na
O Deity, please!
Ten crafts You crafted
in Your language;
Your laws and Your judgments we pronounce
in our language.
Mountains and hills You raised
in Your language;
God of gods, we bless You
in our language.
An eternal structure You built
in Your language;
let me expound riddles, so we praise You
in our language.
The Temple’s furnishings You set
in Your language;
quickly, my people, let us laud
in our language.
Thus said the High and Lofty
in Your language;
Noah accepted that we acknowledge You
in our language.
You made the people’s elders wise
in Your language;
if we speak let us tell Your praises
in our language.
Ḥay-v-Qayyam
Living and enduring, awesome and high and holy.
Said Rabbi Yonatan,
in Beit Guvrin he gave an utterance:
Four are the great languages.
Know them, linguists, to speak them.
The first is the language of the Greeks,
which is good for song and chants.
Its hymnody reddens the face;
but sin and heretical books come after it.
The battle-defiled masters of Rome
came down in war against my people.
They wrote in the Edomite language,
their language to harm my warrior.
Eulogies and wailing? Aramaic.
Let us cry at the burial of a fellow.
Syriac for rhetorical commemoration
at the hand of the Dealer of Life and Death.
Twice in love we say the Shema’,
Your saying refined in the language of the Hebrews.
Our voices we will raise in the Holy Tongue,
the first of Your words — “Let light be” — illuminate.
Thus four great languages
powerful are they in reading aloud.
The sages taught us what they signify.
Elders of the people — may their souls ascend!
El-Na
O Deity, please
forever be adored
and forever be sanctified
and forever and ever reign and be exalted,
Sovereign Deity, awesome and high and holy.
For You are Sovereign, Sovereign of sovereigns;
Your reign is eternal.
Converse of THEIR Wonders;
tell THEIR strength;
may THEIR forces glorify THEM, sanctify THEM, exalt THEM,
hymn, song, laudation, awesome praises of THEIR glory.
Qiqlar
The seventy translated;
the knowing ones said;
changing in Greek until pleasant;
holy!
To an unclear speech
Ptolmey ordered to translate the Teaching.
Bless the covenant’s guardian and light’s creator;
holy!
The 1st correction:
God created in the beginning
lest it come to his mind
the Deity was created at the beginning.
The seventy translated;
the knowing ones said;
changing in Greek until pleasant;
holy!
The 2nd change:
I will make humanity
lest it come to his mind
that creation was of two forces, in folly.
To an unclear speech
Ptolmey ordered to translate the Teaching.
Bless the covenant’s guardian and light’s creator;
holy!
The 3rd idea:
And he finished on the sixth
lest it come to his mind
that THEY worked on the quiet day.
The seventy translated;
the knowing ones said;
changing in Greek until pleasant;
holy!
The 4th reading:
Male and female THEY created him.
lest it come to his mind
that THEY made him in two bodies.
To an unclear speech
Ptolmey ordered to translate the Teaching.
Bless the covenant’s guardian and light’s creator;
holy!
The 5th form:
Come, I will descend and babble
lest it come to his mind
that THEY came with others to Babel.
The seventy translated;
the knowing ones said;
changing in Greek until pleasant;
holy!
The 6th exegesis:
And Sarah laughted with her fellows
lest it come to his mind
that the Ancient hates her thoughts.
To an unclear speech
Ptolmey ordered to translate the Teaching.
Bless the covenant’s guardian and light’s creator;
holy!
The 7th matter:
And in their desire dug a trough
lest it come to his mind
that the righteous sinned irredeemably.
The seventy translated;
the knowing ones said;
changing in Greek until pleasant;
holy!
The 8th scription:
On people-carriers
lest it come to his mind
that a donkey befit his purpose.
To an unclear speech
Ptolmey ordered to translate the Teaching.
Bless the covenant’s guardian and light’s creator;
holy!
The 9th rhetoric:
And in other lands
lest it come to his mind
they were defiled only in that land.
The seventy translated;
the knowing ones said;
changing in Greek until pleasant;
holy!
The 10th utterance:
The elect of the children of Israel
lest it come to his mind
only the lads of Israel were upright.
To an unclear speech
Ptolmey ordered to translate the Teaching.
Bless the covenant’s guardian and light’s creator;
holy!
The 11th teaching:
The hairy-footed one
lest it come to his mind
“they insulted my sweet-eyed wife!”
The seventy translated;
the knowing ones said;
changing in Greek until pleasant;
holy!
The 12th buttress:
Not one precious thing of theirs
lest it come to his mind
that he merited only their donkey.
To an unclear speech
Ptolmey ordered to translate the Teaching.
Bless the covenant’s guardian and light’s creator;
holy!
The 13th reading:
I did not command to serve them
lest it come to his mind
were they made, I did not create their standing.
The seventy translated;
the knowing ones said;
changing in Greek until pleasant;
holy!
To an unclear speech
Ptolmey ordered to translate the Teaching.
Bless the covenant’s guardian and light’s creator;
holy!
Rahit
And so...
And they read in the book, in the teaching of God, explained,
and giving it sense, they understood the scripture.
And they read, —
the seniors,
righteous ones, and interpreters;
laws and rulings they read for us,
In the book —
of the servant,
whose Master granted a boon;
the God of Eternity granted for us.
In the teaching of —
holiness
are written words inexplicable.
Lo, the Translator translates for us.
God —
desires their clarity.
Please, do not skip between verses!
Fathers of the translation clarified for us.
Explained, —
quick was the heart
of the proselyte in whom was wisdom;
from Rome came Onkelos as help for us.
And giving it —
and set for the fivefold;
truly upright was his strength
upon the inheritance that Moses gave for us.
Sense, —
wisdom, and understanding,
Jonathan merited receiving comprehension;
prophetic readings he translated for us.
They understood, —
Onkelos and Jonathan,
legends and stories of the mighty,
sweet to publicize them publicly for us.
The scripture —
and oral law,
in which good and proper truths are found;
from our sages came verity for us.
Silluq
And so, and to You holiness ascends,
for You are the Holy One and Savior of Israel.
BeLT-CoCooN-No-SPaM
is the mnemonic to readings befitting a translator.
The transgression of “what is before and what is after”
does not stop the translation of the beginning of light and dark.
There is no problem on account of the merit of the mighty one;
we translate what Lot did to those girls.
Tamar and Judah is a matter in his merit,
for he confessed and sought forgiveness for his sin.
The first matter of the calf is translated and read,
for the stiff-necked people will return and revere.
The curses and blessings are read and translated;
let not the soft hearts of the community melt!
Punishments are read and translated,
do not worry lest the people believe out of fear.
Amnon and Tamar, as well as Absalom’s battle,
are read without concern that it tarnishes the diamond.
The paramour at Gibeah, her matter we will remember,
for perhaps there will be hope from the valley of trouble.
“Make known” last, but Rabbi Eliezer
says that to read it is to cast down the crown.
So too are there readings which are forbidden to translate,
and so we can remember them, the mnemonic is RoC-PaD-oN.
Reuben’s matter is not translated,
until “the children of Jacob” for whom it was turned to a lake.
The second calf — one must be careful,
for Aaron erred in calling gold quick.
The priestly blessing — could the one God turn THEIR face?
THEY do not turn THEIR face or accept bribes.
David and Amnon, no, but what about Tamar?
Don’t translate if the verse says “Amnon son of David.”
Read it refinedly whenever it is written rudely,
to honor the Torah that the CAUSE gave.
Repeat, recompensors, to teach and to read “he will sleep with her.”
Eyes here learn that “tumors” they will see.
Sin on your head immediately if you didn’t say “dung.”
A gift in a grandchild’s hand is producing from leg-water.
Come, we will see that difficult is the labor
that the translator volunteers for he has mercy on the community.
And not to mention the lector,
who must pronounce the words of awe.
Each and every one of them are human beings,
not fire-angels but flesh and blood.
Meanwhile the messenger-angels and the holy snake-angels,
and the mount-angels and the beast-angels of the holy chariot —
of whose matter we do not conclude for it is holy,
though some conclude with it on the holy pilgrimage of assembly —
and the attendant-angels and lion-angels and all the holy creature-angels
call one to another in the trisagion in holiness.
As is written by the hand of Your prophet...

tei:note.tei:p: According to the rabbinic schema, there are seventy nations on earth, each with its own language.
Abraham, who according to rabbinic legend preserved the primordially-spoken Hebrew lost from other nations.
Linguistic terms
According to midrash, Malachi and Ezra were the same person.
Much of the midrashic material found in this piyyut is derived from Yerushalmi Megillah 1:9:4.
According to Yerushalmi Megillah 1:9:4, Ezra would have merited to receive the Torah if it had not already been given.
These three words in Aramaic.
Nehemiah
The Levites
Persia, based on the imagery of Daniel.

According to a legend recorded in Bavli Yoma 69a, High Priest Shimon the Righteous greeted Alexander the Great clad in his priestly garb, despite the fact it was normally forbidden outside of the Temple area.
Alexander the Great is rumored to have been buried in a golden sarcophagus full of honey, a method of preservation known as mellification.

The Library of Alexandria. Much of this portion is based on the legend of the Septuagint’s translation found in the apocryphal Letter of Aristeas, as well as the variants of said legend found in rabbinic texts.
Israel, based on a verse from Hosea.
Alexander.
Literally: “heart.” The heart is the source of knowledge and understanding in Jewish traditional anatomy.
According to Bavli Shabbat 31b, the word hen, here translated as “lo,” can be interpreted as the Greek word for ”one” — ἕν. This dual meaning is referenced in the piyyut itself.
Pirkei Avot 5:1 — in ten utterances the word was created.
Psalm 78:2
Isaiah 57:15
One of the seven laws of Noah is the prohibition of idolatry.
This entire piyyut is an elaboration of the midrash of four languages found (among other locations) in Yerushalmi Megillah 1:9:3
Bavli Ḥagiga 15b claims that Aḥer (Elisha ben Abuya) was tempted to heresy through Greek songs.
Latin, the language for battle.
The mystics claim that the earth was created in Hebrew.

This piyyut lists the thirteen changes made in the Septuagint according to the midrash found (among other locations) in Masechet Sofrim 1:8, Bavli Megillah 9a, and Yerushalmi Megillah 1:9:13. Not all of these alterations are found in the Septuagint as we know it, but some of them (such as the third, eighth, ninth, and twelfth) are.
Rather than “In the beginning created God.” Genesis 1:1
Literally: “heart.” The heart is the source of knowledge and understanding in Jewish traditional anatomy.
Rather than “Let us make humanity.” Genesis 1:26
Rather than “on the seventh.” Genesis 2:2
Shabbat.
Rather than “created them.” Genesis 2:5.
The primordial human, who was created according to both rabbinic legend and Greek philosophy as both male and female.
Rather than “let us descend and babble.” Genesis 11:7
Rather than “within herself.” Genesis 18:12
Abraham wasn’t rebuked but Sarah was, although they both laughed. The rabbis say that this is because Abraham privately laughed, but Sarah laughed in public, which is more shameful.
As opposed to “they killed a man... maimed an ox,” the midrash reads “they killed an ox... dug a trough.” Genesis 49:6

As opposed to “on a donkey.” Exodus 4:20. The censorship of donkey imagery with regards to Moses, also found in the twelfth alteration, might be related to the common accusation in classical-era Egypt that the Jews were donkey-worshippers. While not all of the alterations found in this midrash are attested, both of the donkey censorships are.
As opposed to merely mentioning Egypt. Exodus 12:40
In Egypt the people Israel descended to impurity. But the math doesn’t add up if it’s just Egypt.
As opposed to “the youths.” Exodus 24:5. The midrash also includes Exodus 24:11 with the same replacement.
As opposed to “the hare.” Leviticus 11:6. Rabbinic legend states that Ptolemy’s wife was named Arnevet. In fact, the first Ptolemy’s father was named Lagos, or “rabbit.”
As opposed to “one donkey of theirs.” Numbers 16:15.
As opposed to “I did not command them.” Deuteronomy 17:3. The midrash also includes Deuteronomy 4:19 with the addition of “to illuminate,” both to clarify that God has power over celestial bodies.
Nehemiah 8:8
Moses
Onkelos, author of the canonical targum of the Torah, is said to have been a proselyte originating from an imperial family.
The Torah
Jonathan son of Uzziel, author of the canonical targum of the Prophets.
The following piyyut is largely based on the instructions for the translator found in the Bavli, from Megillah 25a to the end of the chapter.
Obviously not the same as the Hebrew mnemonic, but the same function — each consonant reflects a different following narrative.
The following passages are both read and translated, despite the fact they may seem inappropriate for translation.
Esoteric matters which rabbinically are forbidden from public discussion: what is above and what is below, what is before and what is after
Genesis 1:1-3
Abraham
Genesis 19
Exodus 32:1-6
II Samuel 13
II Samuel 15-18
David
Judges 19
See Lamentations 3:29 and Hosea 2:17
Ezekiel 16

Bavli Megillah 25b. Rabbi Eliezer was opposed to the recitation of Ezekiel 16 as a haftara. Once when in the presence of a reader who began to read it he responded, “Before making known Jerusalem’s abominations, make known your mother’s.”
Not the same as the Hebrew mnemonic, see prior note.
Genesis 35:22, which has a paragraph break within it. The translator exclusively translates the portion after the paragraph break — “and the children of Jacob were twelve.”
See Psalm 114:8
Exodus 32:21-25. Here Aaron, due to lack fo care, says “the calf came out,” which implies that the calf could move of its own volition.
Numbers 6:24-26. The idea of God turning THEIR face would imply partiality and unfairness if read literally.
See Deuteronomy 10:17

This is an example of the halakhic form known as an ukimta — resolving a contradiction by limiting the scope. The baraita says to translate the story of Amnon, but the mishnah says not to, so the ukimta suggests the mishna is speaking specifically of the phrase “Amnon son of David” in II Samuel 13:1

This portion of the piyyut relies on nearly untranslatable wordplay to allude to the impolite word written out and not read. This phrase implies the root shin-gimel-lamed, which literally means “to fuck” but is read as “to sleep with.”
This phrase implies the root ayin-peh-lamed, which literally means “hemorrhoids” but is read as “tumors.”
This phrase implies the root ḥet-resh-yod, which literally means “shit” but is read as “dung.”
This phrase implies the root shin-yod-nun, which literally means “piss” but is read as “leg’s water.”
Ezekiel 1
Shavuot. Nowadays every rabbinic Jewish community recites Ezekiel 1 as the haftara on Shavuot, according to the minority opinion of Rabbi Yehuda who permits it.
